body.p: Reconsideration is respectfully requested. Claims 1-11, 13-16, and 18-20 are pending. Claims 12 and 17 remain canceled without prejudice. No new matter has been introduced. For the reasons set forth below, it is respectfully submitted that the pending claims are allowable.

Claims 1-6 and 8-10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being allegedly unpatentable over US20160022221 ("Ou") in view of CN108544925 ("Xiong"). See 8/5/24 NFOA at 3-7. Claim 7 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being allegedly unpatentable over Ou in view of Xiong and further in view of W002058537 ("Heller"). See id. at 7. Claims 11, 13-16, and 18-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being allegedly unpatentable over Ou in view of Xiong and further in view of U.S. Publ. No. 2016/0296148 ("Hayter"). See id. at 7-11. For the reasons set forth below, it is respectfully submitted that the cited references, either alone or in combination, do not render the pending claims obvious.
A. Xiong is Not Properly Combinable with Ou

First, it is respectfully submitted that the cited references do not render the pending claims obvious because Xiong is not properly combinable with Ou. In particular, Xiong is non-analogous art. It is well-established law that art is non-analogous unless it is: (1) from the same field of endeavor as the claimed invention; or (2) reasonably pertinent to the particular problem faced by the inventor. In re Bigio, 381 F.3d 1320, 1325 (Fed. Cir. 2004); In re Wood and Eversole, 599 F.2d 1032, 1036 (CCPA 1979). Moreover, art is "reasonably pertinent" to a particular problem when it would "logically commend itself' to an inventor's attention in considering the problem at hand. In re Icon Health and Fitness, Inc., 496 F.3d 1374, 1379-80 (Fed. Cir. 2007) (citing In re Clay, 966 F.2d 656, 658-59 (Fed. Cir. 1992)); see also MPEP § 2141.01(a). Conversely, when art is directed to a different purpose than a claimed invention, an inventor would have less motivation or occasion to consider it. See In re Clay, 966 F.2d at 658-59.

Here, Xiong is directed to a battery management system of an electric automobile. Xiong at 2. By contrast, the embodiments of the present application comprise "systems, devices and methods for detecting a sensor fault in an analyte sensor." U.S. Publ. No. 2021/0219879 ("the '879 Publication"), Abstract. As such, it is respectfully submitted that Xiong encompasses subject matter

from a completely different field of endeavor than the embodiments of the present application. With respect to the particular problem being solved, Xiong focuses on utilizing a high real-time vehicle battery management unit and a cloud computing system based on battery history data to address issues with the incomplete functionality of battery management systems in electric vehicles. See Xiong at 2. By contrast, the embodiments of the present application are designed to solve the problem of detecting sensor faults in analyte sensors using one or more calculated metrics, and one or more thresholds based on the calculated metrics. See '879 Publication, Para. [0008]. Thus, Xiong neither addresses the same problem nor serves the same purpose as the analyte monitoring systems or the methods of the current claims. Xiong would not have logically commended itself to Applicants' attention as being analogous.

Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that Xiong is neither from the same field of endeavor as the claimed subject matter, nor is Xiong's battery management system reasonably pertinent to the problem faced by the embodiments of the instant application. See In re Bigio, 381 F.3d at 1325. As such, it is not properly combinable with Ou, and it is respectfully requested that the Section 103 rejections be withdrawn.
B. The Cited References, Alone or in Combination, Fail to Teach, Describe or Suggest
the Claimed Subject Matter of Independent Claims 1 and 13.

Second, even assuming arguendo that the cited references are properly combinable (which they are not), it is respectfully submitted that they do not teach, describe, or suggest all of the limitations of independent claims 1 and 13.
Independent claims 1 and 13, recite (with emphasis added):

1. An analyte monitoring system, comprising: a sensor control device including an analyte sensor at least a portion of which is configured to be inserted into a user's body, first processing circuitry, and a first
non-transitory memory, wherein the sensor control device is configured to collect
sensor data indicative of an analyte level from the analyte sensor; and
a reader device comprising a second processing circuitry and a second non- transitory memory,
wherein at least one of the first or the second non-transitory memory includes instructions that, when executed, cause the at least one of the first or the second
processing circuitry to:
calculate a rate of change metric based on the collected sensor data, wherein the rate of change metric is calculated at a first time;
calculate a sum of analyte levels metric based on the collected sensor data, wherein the sum of analyte levels metric is calculated at a second time;
compare the rate of change metric with a first threshold and compare the sum of analyte levels metric with a second threshold; and
in response to a determination that the rate of change metric exceeds the first threshold, that the sum of analyte levels metric exceeds the second threshold, and
that a difference between the first time and the second time is less than a
predetermined time threshold, generate an indication of a sensor fault.
13. A computer-implemented method for detecting a sensor fault, the method comprising:
collecting, by a sensor control device comprising an analyte sensor at least a portion of which is inserted into a user's body, sensor data indicative of an analyte
level;
calculating a rate of change metric based on the collected sensor data, wherein the rate of change metric is calculated at a first time;
calculating a sum of analyte levels metric based on the collected sensor data, wherein the sum of analyte levels metric is calculated at a second time;
comparing the rate of change metric with a first threshold and comparing the sum of analyte levels metric with a second threshold; and
in response to determining that the rate of change metric exceeds the first threshold, that the sum of analyte levels metric exceeds the second threshold, and
that a difference between the first time and the second time is less than a predetermined time threshold, generating an indication of the sensor fault.

It is respectfully submitted that the cited references fail to disclose generating an indication of sensor fault in response to determining "that a difference between the first time and the second time is less than a predetermined time threshold."

The 8/5/24 NFOA acknowledges that "Ou does not explicitly teach that an indication of a sensor fault is generated when a difference between the first time and the second time is less than a predetermined time threshold." 8/5/24 NFOA at 5. The 8/5/24 NFOA relies on Xiong for allegedly disclosing this limitation. Id. Specifically, the 8/5/24 NFOA cites to paragraph 3 of page 6 of Xiong, which states: "fault type judging module, a single current sensor value exceeds the current threshold, the monomer battery voltage sensor value exceeds the voltage threshold value and the monomer battery temperature sensor value exceeds a temperature threshold value exceeds a temperature

threshold in any one condition is satisfied and the duration time exceeds the time threshold, then the module output is suspected a sensor fault." Id. While Xiong mentions "a time threshold" and "the duration time exceeds the time threshold," Xiong is silent regarding generating a sensor fault in response to determining a difference between the first time and the second time is less than a predetermined time threshold.

The remaining references are cited for other purposes, and do not teach, describe or suggest the claim limitation "in response to a determination . . . that a difference between the first time and the second time is less than a predetermined time threshold, generate an indication of a sensor fault."
Accordingly, the cited references, either alone or in combination, fail to disclose all of the limitations of independent claims 1 and 13, and it is requested that the Section 103 rejection to claims
1 and 13 be withdrawn, as well as to all claims that depend therefrom.

Amendments to and/or cancellations of the claims are made without prejudice and solely to clarify the issues before the Examiner and/or to advance prosecution of this application and do not constitute a defacto acquiescence to any objection and/or rejection. Accordingly, this response does not concede that previously pending claims are not patentable.

The right is reserved to pursue claims to any subject matter supported by the disclosure of this application in one or more continuation and/or divisional applications at a later time, including the subject matter of any previously pending claims regardless of whether those claims were amended or cancelled herein. This may entail the pursuit of broader claims, narrower claims, and subject matter that was previously relinquished by virtue of argument or amendment.

Any silence with regard to the rejections of and/or objections to certain dependent claims constitutes a recognition that such are moot based on amendments or remarks made with respect to the independent claim from which the dependent claims depend. Such silence does not constitute a defacto acquiescence to any objection and/or rejection.

In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully submitted that all claims are in allowable form.
